LESSON: READING 4.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: DIALOGUE

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.2: Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue, part of Strand 4 in Grade 5 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: What do you consider when selecting materials from the library? 2. How can we ensure peace with others in the face of conflict?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. conduct a reader’s theatre to practice reading dialogues based on the theme,

2. make short notes on key events from the dialogues read,

3. work jointly to pick out vocabulary from the texts and build a vocabulary bank,

4. use the dictionary to find the meaning of vocabulary identified,

5. collaborate with peers to use a dictionary or other sources to search for synonyms of the words,

6. work with peers to compose simple poems, songs or plays on peace building using the vocabulary identified,

7. team up with peers to organise an indigenous languages peace mini- festival project to stage the plays, poems and songs, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. conduct a reader’s theatre to practice reading dialogues based on the theme,
2. make short notes on key events from the dialogues read,
3. work jointly to pick out vocabulary from the texts and build a vocabulary bank,
4. use the dictionary to find the meaning of vocabulary identified,
5. collaborate with peers to use a dictionary or other sources to search for synonyms of the words,
6. work with peers to compose simple poems, songs or plays on peace building using the vocabulary identified,
7. team up with peers to organise an indigenous languages peace mini- festival project to stage the plays, poems and songs, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 4.2.1 Extensive Reading: Dialogue together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: This is promoted as the learner effectively orders and prioritises tasks when working with peers to organise an

indigenous languages peace mini- festival project to stage the plays, poems and songs.

• Learning to Learn: This is developed as the learner builds on their learning experiences when using the dictionary to find

synonyms and meaning of vocabulary and creates a personal word bank.

Values:
• Respect: This is nurtured as the learner ensures positive regard for others by adhering and observing library rules when

conducting a reader’s theatre to practice reading dialogues based on the theme.

• Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner cooperates with peers to compose simple poems, songs or plays on peace

building.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Nationalism: This is promoted as the learner reads materials on peace building for general information.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept on the use of reference materials like the dictionary to their learning of similar

resources in English.
